solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A measure to restrict trade is arranged between banks

indicators.note: to restrict means to hem in, so the measure surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: MM is a millimetre, a measure of length

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of trade and is are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A trade barrier is being negotiated between banks, as in finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests money and trade barriers, but these are a river's banks; MM for millimetre is a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a river lies between its two banks.

clue.text: Priest finds organ unserviceable

parts.note: an organ is a publication such as a magazine, shortened to mag

explanation.surface: A clergyman discovers his church organ is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like a church instrument but is a newspaper or magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus was a member of the ancient Persian priestly caste.

clue.text: Security guards on honour

indicators.note: guards means encloses protectively, so the security word wraps the other piece

parts.note: defence means protection or security
RE means on or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Security staff keep watch over an honour or award.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is the respect or honour shown to someone.

clue.text: See 11 across
New bakery product boxes, not coded

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the pastry holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: an eclair is a cream-filled pastry

explanation.surface: A new pastry is packed into boxes, with no secret about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun but is a verb: ECLAIR contains N.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair is a French phrase for a message sent in plain language, without encryption.

clue.text: 21 needs an hour to get into the spirit

indicators.note: to get into means to enter, so the hour phrase goes inside the spirit word

parts.note: mood means temper or spirit

explanation.surface: Peter needs an hour before he can get into the spirit of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is PETER (21 down); both that word and this answer are slang for the male member. Reading 21 as the age of majority is tempting, but the slang link is the setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang euphemisms for the penis.

clue.text: Icy river escapade curtailed

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a lark is a prank or escapade

explanation.surface: A frolic on a frozen river is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' drops the K from LARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar regions are freezing, so polar describes extreme cold.

clue.text: Parking sign somewhat to the left?

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to ink a deal is to sign it

explanation.surface: A parking sign seems to point a bit to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' describes politics mildly left-wing, a paler shade of red; the question mark admits the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink describes someone with mildly socialist leanings, short of being red.

clue.text: West Indian cricketer stops victor being immature

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the cricketer's name is plugged with the letter

parts.note: Brian Lara is a famous batsman from Trinidad
V is Victor in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A West Indies cricketer halts a winner who is still a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'victor' goes inside LARA.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is an insect in its juvenile stage, before adult form.

clue.text: Jogger welcomes a rest

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the jogger word takes the letter inside

parts.note: a jogger is something that jogs the memory, a reminder

explanation.surface: A runner pauses to take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' looks like a runner, but it jogs the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Some lifting affects boob

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Weight training has an effect on one's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a blunder or embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Sister has cracked fish — weird anagram

indicators.note: has cracked means has broken into, so the nun goes inside the fish

parts.note: cod is a fish
a nun is a religious sister
rum means odd or weird

explanation.surface: A nun breaks into a fish, which is a strange puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anagram' is used loosely as a word puzzle or riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a riddle or puzzle, of which a letter-shuffle is one kind.

clue.text: West Indian batsman said, of life, that playing the game leads to natural selection

indicators.note: said signals the batsman's title and name are heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: Sir Viv Richards, the Antiguan batsman

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the following words frolic into a new order

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Sir Viv Richards remarks on life that playing the game is Darwinian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges OF LIFE THAT into ALOFTHEFIT; the Test nods back to cricket. The sound of SIR VIV matches only the opening of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Survival of the fittest is Herbert Spencer's phrase for Darwin's evolutionary mechanism.

clue.text: "Cheers" players in old US sitcom

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
XI is a team of eleven players, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: The cast of Cheers appearing in a vintage American comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is itself an old US sitcom, a decoy for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi was an American comedy series about New York cab drivers, running 1978-83.

clue.text: See 22 across
Car going round province's track

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the car surrounds the province

parts.note: a motor is a car
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A car laps a regional racing circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a racetrack but is a verb, to keep watch on.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to keep track of it, observing over time.

clue.text: What mush swirls around ought to be this?

definitions.text: What mush swirls around ought to be this?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the zero
swirls describes the letters of what mush being stirred into a new order

parts.note: ought is a variant of nought, zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking what mushy stuff one swishes round the mouth should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swirls' rearranges WHAT MUSH, and 'around' places it round O. The whole clue also describes rinsing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is swirled round the mouth to freshen breath.

clue.text: Villain backed by guy in France, of course

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the villain word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel
a guy is a rope used to steady a tent, a cord

explanation.surface: A rogue supported by a fellow Frenchman, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' turns CAD into DAC. 'Guy' is a guy rope, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: D'accord is the French expression for agreed or certainly.

clue.text: Surpassed UK on trade supply

indicators.note: supply is read as supplely, in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Britain beat others in trade supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not a noun but an adverb from supple, flagging the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrank someone is to hold a higher position, to surpass them.

clue.text: Universal and mostly pliable tool

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: tensile can mean capable of being stretched, pliable

explanation.surface: A versatile and flexible implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the final E from TENSILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Posh B&B in secure Texas city

indicators.note: in places the posh letter and the lodging inside the fastening word

parts.note: to lock is to secure
U means upper-class, posh
BB stands for bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: A smart guesthouse in a safe Texas town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubbock is a city in northwest Texas, birthplace of Buddy Holly.

clue.text: One with tip possibly heading right?

definitions.text: One with tip possibly heading right?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of one and tip may be put another way
heading means the first letter of the word right

explanation.surface: Something with a sharp end, perhaps aimed rightward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges ONE TIP into POINTE, then the first letter of 'right' adds R. The whole clue describes an arrow cursor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a stick or arrow ending in a point that indicates direction.

clue.text: Fix zip to limit introduction of birth control measure?

indicators.note: to limit means to bound or hem in, so the pieces surround the letter

parts.note: to place something is to fix it in position
zip means nothing, zero, the letter O

indicators.note: introduction of means the first letter of birth

explanation.surface: Setting a zip to hold back a contraceptive method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birth control' reads as one phrase, but 'birth' gives only B and 'control measure' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy treatment given to the control group in a drug trial.

clue.text: Advert for some mushy peas

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Promotion for a portion of mashed peas.
explanation.walkthrough: Mushy peas are a British side dish of mashed marrowfat peas.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant publicity or promotion.

clue.text: Safe title initially secured by Law Lord?

indicators.note: secured by means held fast within, so the letter goes inside the lord

parts.note: a Law Lord sat in the House of Lords as a peer

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of title

explanation.surface: A safe title, granted first to a senior judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a peter is criminals' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is underworld slang for a strongbox, as in peterman, a safecracker.

clue.text: Poem changing 5's alphabetical order

indicators.note: changing says the whole pool of letters is altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: 5 is 5 down, manhood, with an s added for the possessive

indicators.note: order, read as a verb on the word before it, says the letters of alphabetical are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: A poem altering the alphabetical order of five.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 points to 5 down, and its 's here supplies a real S. 'Order' rearranges ALPHABETICAL and 'changing' shuffles that with MANHOODS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is John Dryden's 1681 political satire in verse.

clue.text: Keen to see good in bad

indicators.note: in places the letter for good inside the word for bad

parts.note: dire means very bad

explanation.surface: Eager to find the good in bad things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager but is the verb to wail for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to lament, and a dirge is a mournful lament for the dead.

clue.text: What a sailor may call a cyclist

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a Scottish Olympic track cyclist

explanation.surface: How a seaman might hail someone on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Hoy won six Olympic golds in track cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use this greeting to hail another ship.

clue.text: Salt coating long single cut of beef

indicators.note: coating means covering, so the sailor surrounds the longing

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, an AB or able seaman
to long is to itch for something
single means one

explanation.surface: Salting a long single cut of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is a sailor, AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitchbone is the rump bone of cattle, or the joint cut from it.

clue.text: I walk 27 kilometres in this, then run

indicators.note: in signals that the abbreviation goes inside the 27 word

parts.note: 27 across is hurry, and hie is an old word for hurry
K is short for kilometres
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: I walk twenty-seven kilometres in this, then I run.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer speaks: 'I walk'. HIE (hurry, the answer at 27) contains K.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is someone who walks long distances for pleasure.

clue.text: Expedition dish that's hot instead of cold

indicators.note: instead of signals one letter takes another's place, hot H for cold C

parts.note: curry is a spiced dish

explanation.surface: A trek meal that's hot rather than cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is H and 'cold' is C, as on taps. 'Expedition' looks like a journey but means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, a sense shared by haste.

clue.text: Extremely keen wiseacre's keenness for letters?

indicators.note: Extremely means the outermost letters of keen

parts.note: an owl is a wise person, a wiseacre
edge means sharpness, keenness

explanation.surface: A know-all's enthusiasm for literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' means learning, as in a man of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters means scholarship or learning, which is acquired information.
